sections.h2: How does selling a house in Moses Lake work?
sections.html:
A Moses Lake owner can list with an agent, sell without one, or take a cash offer from a buyer who purchases the house as-is. The paperwork is the same in every case: a deed, a state excise tax affidavit, and recording through Grant County.

Moses Lake is the most populous city in Grant County, and the Census Bureau estimates 27,469 residents as of July 1, 2025. That is up from 20,366 in 2010 and 25,146 in 2020. The city spreads over about 18 square miles of land around a lake with three arms, and the lake sits in the middle of town. A cash sale tends to appeal to sellers with inherited houses, rentals, or repair lists who would rather skip showings and move on a date they choose.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Moses Lake housing?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau puts the median owner-occupied value at $310,000 and the owner-occupied rate at 61.2 percent for 2020 to 2024.

sections.h2: What shapes the Moses Lake economy and commute?
sections.html:
Agriculture built the city, and manufacturing and technology now sit beside it. Boeing uses the Grant County International Airport as a test and evaluation facility, and the former air base grounds also hold Big Bend Community College.

  • Interstate 90 and State Route 17 bypass the city center, while State Route 171 and Interstate 90 Business serve downtown.
  • Grant Transit Authority runs bus routes in the city and to Ephrata and nearby towns.
  • The Columbia Basin Railroad is based in Moses Lake and is the busiest shortline railroad in Eastern Washington.
  • Manufacturers of electric vehicle batteries have factories or research sites here, drawn by hydroelectric power and nearby silicon processors.

The Census Bureau reports a mean travel time to work of 18.2 minutes for Moses Lake workers, a figure worth quoting to buyers who commute.

sections.h2: How is Moses Lake laid out, and why does the lake matter to a seller?
sections.html:
The lake runs more than 18 miles across its three arms and has over 120 miles of shoreline, so the city has a lot of waterfront property. South of town are Potholes Reservoir and the Columbia National Wildlife Refuge.

The lake was a smaller, shallower body of water until it was dammed in the early 1900s and folded into the Columbia Basin Project. The area had few residents before Moses Lake Army Air Base opened in 1942, and irrigation water from Grand Coulee Dam arrived in 1955. The town of Westlake, platted in 1945 and incorporated in 1958, was annexed into Moses Lake in 1972. Elevation is about 1,060 feet. Public schools belong to the Moses Lake School District, which runs eleven elementary schools, three middle schools, and Moses Lake High School along with several alternative programs.

sections.h2: Which Moses Lake permits can trip up a sale?
sections.html:
Any structure work done without the permit the city requires is the usual problem. The Building Department publishes a list of permit types, and a buyer or title company may ask whether your fence, porch, or roof had one.

  • Fences: a permit is required before installing any fence.
  • Re-roofing: a residential re-roof that replaces more than 25 percent of the sheathing needs a permit, and solar roof panels need one.
  • Retaining walls: a permit applies at 4 feet or higher, measured from the bottom of the footing.
  • Covered porches: a building permit is required for an attached covered porch of 200 square feet or more.
  • Remodels, additions, and accessory dwelling units: submitted through the city's permit portal with plans.
  • Demolition and grading or clearing: each has its own permit.

Call the Moses Lake Building Department at 509-764-3743 if you are unsure about a past project. If something was built without a permit, ask the department how it can be documented before you list.

sections.h2: Can a buyer run a short-term rental in a Moses Lake house?
sections.html:
Only with city approval, and the approval does not follow the house to a new owner. Chapter 15.650 of the Moses Lake Municipal Code regulates stays of less than 30 days and allows them in specified zoning districts.

An owner applies to the Community Development Department for a short-term rental endorsement, and a business license under Chapter 5.04 is not issued until the endorsement is approved. The city says endorsements are generally not transferable, so a buyer who wants to rent the home by the night should expect to apply again after closing. If you currently run the house as a short-term rental, tell any buyer that the endorsement may not carry over.

sections.h2: What are the excise tax and recording steps in Moses Lake?
sections.html:
The seller files a Real Estate Excise Tax Affidavit, pays the tax to the Grant County Treasurer, and the deed is then recorded. The Department of Revenue says the tax is due on the date of sale, which is the date the deed is notarized, even if recording happens later.

The state portion is graduated: 1.1 percent on the first $525,000 under the thresholds in force through December 31, 2026, with 1.28 percent, 2.75 percent, and 3 percent above higher breakpoints. The local rate is added to it. Sales closing in 2027 use breakpoints of $551,000, $1,551,000, and $3,051,000. The Grant County Treasurer is at 35 C Street NW, Room 204, in Ephrata, phone 509-754-2010, open weekdays from 8 a.m. to noon and 1 to 5 p.m. The county's page links the current state affidavit forms for sales on or after May 1, 2026, and it lists April 30 as the deadline for the first half of the year's property taxes. Ask the treasurer how current-year taxes are handled at your closing.

Washington also requires a seller disclosure statement on improved residential property, delivered within five business days of mutual acceptance unless waived or exempt, under RCW 64.06.020.

sections.h2: When does a cash offer make sense in Moses Lake?
sections.html:
It makes sense when the house needs work, a tenant or relative is still inside, or you need a firm closing date. Rentals with worn finishes and inherited homes that nobody wants to renovate are common examples.

Ask any Moses Lake buyer for proof of funds, a written closing date, and a clear statement of who pays the excise tax and title costs. Then price your own timeline: a listing takes preparation, showings, and a buyer's inspection and financing, while a cash sale can close when you are ready. Request an offer on your Moses Lake address and compare the net to what a listing would leave after excise tax, agent fees, and repairs.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to sell a Moses Lake house?
faqs.a: No permit is needed to sell. The city requires permits for work such as fences, re-roofs that replace more than 25 percent of the sheathing, retaining walls of 4 feet or more, and covered porches of 200 square feet or more. If past work lacked a permit, contact the Building Department at 509-764-3743 before listing.

faqs.q: Who pays the real estate excise tax in Moses Lake?
faqs.a: The seller usually pays. The Department of Revenue says the buyer is responsible if the seller does not, and unpaid tax can become a lien. It is paid to the Grant County Treasurer on the date of sale, with the local rate added to the state's graduated rate.

faqs.q: Does a short-term rental permit transfer to the buyer in Moses Lake?
faqs.a: Generally no. Moses Lake issues short-term rental endorsements under Chapter 15.650, and the city says they are generally not transferable, so a new owner may need a new endorsement before renting by the night.

faqs.q: How much state excise tax would a $310,000 Moses Lake sale owe?
faqs.a: The state portion is $3,410, which is 1.1 percent of $310,000. That figure is the Census median owner-occupied value for 2020 to 2024. The local excise tax is added, so ask your title officer for the full amount.

faqs.q: Where do I record the deed and file the excise tax affidavit for a Moses Lake property?
faqs.a: Grant County handles both. The treasurer collects the excise tax and links the Department of Revenue affidavit forms, and Washington law requires deeds to be recorded with the county auditor. Call the treasurer at 509-754-2010 to confirm what to bring.
